topStories.headline: Hundreds Pack Fort Mason to Oppose 25-Story Marina Safeway Tower as City Deadline Looms
topStories.dek: A community showdown over Align Real Estate's 790-unit mixed-use tower at 15 Marina Boulevard intensified this week as the San Francisco Planning Department faces an August 1 approval deadline.
topStories.body:
The future of the Marina District's beloved Safeway — and the skyline above it — came to a head Thursday night at Fort Mason, where roughly 250 residents gathered to oppose Align Real Estate's proposal to replace the single-story grocery store at 15 Marina Boulevard with a 25-story, 790-unit residential tower. The packed community meeting underscored the depth of opposition in one of San Francisco's most vocal neighborhoods, even as state housing law has left local officials with limited tools to block the project.

The San Francisco Planning Department issued a notice of conditional eligibility for the project under Assembly Bill 2011 on March 24, 2026, placing the estimated $500 million redevelopment on a legislative fast track. Under that state law, the city is mandated to complete its design review and issue a final decision by August 1, 2026. The 297-foot tower, designed by Miami-based firm Arquitectonica, would be the tallest structure on San Francisco's northern waterfront.

The proposal includes 790 housing units — 86 of them designated affordable or below market rate — along with 485 one-bedroom apartments, 88 studios, 132 two-bedroom units, and 85 three-bedroom units. A rebuilt Safeway grocery store at the base would be roughly 57% larger than the current one. Critics have raised concerns about shadow impacts on Marina Green and Moscone Playground under Proposition K, the seismic vulnerability of the site's landfill foundation, and what they describe as token affordability.

The Marina Community Association has publicly stated it supports housing at the site but has called for a building in the 6-to-8-story range, citing comparable Safeway redevelopments in Bernal Heights, the Outer Richmond, and San Mateo. The opposition movement has also connected to a broader statewide ballot initiative effort targeting California's housing mandates, though that campaign remains in early stages and would need hundreds of thousands of signatures to qualify. The Planning Department's August 1 design-review deadline means a final decision on the project's eligibility is imminent.

topStories.headline: New Six-Story Infill Proposed for Cow Hollow's Lombard Street Under City Density Program
topStories.dek: Plans filed July 14 call for a 65-foot, 15-unit building at 2629 Lombard Street, invoking the city's Housing Choice San Francisco program to achieve density above base zoning.
topStories.body:
A new residential infill project has been proposed for the corner of Lombard and Richardson streets in Cow Hollow, adding to the growing list of development applications reshaping the neighborhood's low-rise corridor. Plans filed on July 14, 2026, call for a six-story, 65-foot building at 2629 Lombard Street that would replace a 1932-era two-story house. Studio 12 Architecture is listed as the designer on the application.

The proposed structure would yield approximately 20,550 square feet spread across 15 units, with a mix of two studios, seven one-bedroom apartments, and six two-bedroom homes. Three of the 15 units would be deed-restricted as affordable housing. The plans do not include any on-site parking, a reflection of the project's transit-accessible location near Lombard Street's busy bus corridor. The application invokes the Housing Choice San Francisco (HC-SF) program, an incentive created under the city's recently passed Family Zoning plan that functions similarly to the State Density Bonus law to allow higher density than base zoning would otherwise permit.

The proposal is the latest in a string of Lombard Street infill projects as developers respond to the city's upzoned height limits in Cow Hollow, which now allow structures of at least 65 feet along the corridor. The area has become a flashpoint in San Francisco's broader housing debate, with the Cow Hollow Association and affiliated organizations arguing that rapid upzoning will displace small businesses and alter the neighborhood's historic character. State law, however, limits local governments' ability to deny projects that comply with applicable zoning and density bonus rules.

topStories.headline: Gashouse Cove Waterfront Park Moves Forward After Rec & Park Commission Approval
topStories.dek: San Francisco's Recreation and Park Commission has given conceptual approval to transform the Marina's long-contaminated Gashouse Cove site into a new 5-acre public waterfront park.
topStories.body:
San Francisco is moving ahead with plans to convert Gashouse Cove in the Marina's East Harbor into a new 5-acre public waterfront park adjacent to Marina Green, following conceptual approval from the Recreation and Park Commission. The project, years in the making, is tied to a remediation settlement with PG&E over pollution from a former coal gasification plant that operated near the harbor for decades.

The approved conceptual plan opens up more of the shoreline for public use, including a community dock for kayaks and nonmotorized boating, expanded Bay Trail access, picnic areas, beach volleyball courts, and landscaped open space. Boat infrastructure is also being reorganized: fewer slips overall, with changes to distribution between the East and West Harbors, and the Gashouse Cove fuel dock relocated near the St. Francis Yacht Club. Officials say fuel service will continue without interruption during construction.

The project stems from a 2021 settlement in which PG&E committed to paying up to $160–$190 million to clean up harbor pollution caused by polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons found in East Harbor sediments. While timelines for construction have not been finalized, the commission's approval marks a significant step toward opening a long-industrialized stretch of waterfront to public use. Some Marina Community Association members have raised concerns about the placement of volleyball courts near Marina Boulevard, and debates over the precise number and location of boat slips are ongoing.

moreNews.headline: Union Street Repaving Included in City's $90M Road Program, Work Slated for Early 2027
moreNews.body: A 29-block stretch of the Marina and Russian Hill centered on Union Street is among the corridors targeted in San Francisco's multi-phase street resurfacing program, with work expected to begin in early 2027 and run through October 2028. The broader program, funded by $33 million in state gas-tax revenue plus additional city allocations, covers nearly $90 million in repaving work citywide over the next two years. A separate 26-block stretch across Chinatown, Nob Hill, and Pacific Heights is also included in the same construction phase. Residents on affected blocks should expect temporary lane restrictions and noise during construction periods.

moreNews.headline: Cow Hollow Real Estate Hits Record Pace as Inventory Stays Tight
moreNews.body: Cow Hollow's housing market entered summer 2026 at a notable pace, with April data showing condo buyers paying an average of 118.3% of list price in the neighborhood, according to Compass market data reported by real estate publication Helena 7x7. The 12-month rolling median house price through early 2026 was $6.45 million, with individual sales reaching as high as $16.8 million. Analysts attribute the frenzy to a collision between scarce inventory — just 835 single-family homes were listed across the entire city as of April 1, roughly 265 fewer than typical for that time of year — and a persistent pool of high-net-worth buyers drawn to Cow Hollow's walkability, historic architecture, and proximity to the Presidio and bay.

moreNews.headline: District 2 Supervisor Race Heads to November General Election
moreNews.body: Supervisor Stephen Sherrill, appointed to the District 2 seat in December 2024 by then-Mayor London Breed after Catherine Stefani was elected to the California State Assembly, is running for a full term this fall. Because Sherrill was appointed rather than elected, his seat was up for vote in the June 2, 2026 primary, and will again be contested in the November 3, 2026 general election. District 2 covers the Marina, Pacific Heights, Cow Hollow, and Presidio Heights neighborhoods — a cluster at the center of some of San Francisco's most contentious housing and development debates this year.

restaurants.description: Chef Dominique Crenn's flagship, the only female-led three-Michelin-star restaurant in the US, serving poetic pescatarian tasting menus inspired by her French upbringing and California's coast.

restaurants.name: Greens Restaurant
restaurants.description: A San Francisco institution since 1979, Greens serves seasonal vegetarian California cuisine with sweeping bay and Golden Gate Bridge views from its Fort Mason waterfront location.
restaurants.address: 2 Marina Blvd, Bldg A, Fort Mason

restaurants.name: A16
restaurants.type: Southern Italian restaurant and wine bar
restaurants.description: A neighborhood mainstay named for the highway connecting Naples to Puglia, serving blistered Neapolitan pizzas, housemade pastas, and an extensive southern Italian wine list.

restaurants.name: Delarosa
restaurants.description: A go-to Marina spot for thin-crust Roman pizzas, craft cocktails, and a convivial Italian-inspired aperitivo hour popular with the neighborhood crowd.

restaurants.name: Causwells
restaurants.description: A Marina staple known for shareable American plates, a well-crafted burger, and a casual bar atmosphere popular for weekend brunch and weeknight dinners.

restaurants.name: Pacific Catch
restaurants.description: A laid-back seafood spot with a Pacific Rim twist, offering everything from fresh fish tacos to poke bowls and sushi-style plates for lunch and dinner.

restaurants.name: Blackwood
restaurants.description: A relaxed Chestnut Street spot serving Thai fusion favorites including red curry, mushroom rolls, and inventive Benedicts at brunch, drawing a loyal neighborhood following.

restaurants.name: Tacolicious
restaurants.description: A beloved local mini-chain known for creative tacos, strong margaritas, and a festive atmosphere that fills up fast on weekend nights along Chestnut Street.

restaurants.name: Balboa Cafe
restaurants.description: A Cow Hollow landmark since 1913, the Balboa Cafe is famed for its legendary burger, lively bar scene, and weekend brunch that packs the room with neighborhood regulars.

restaurants.name: Horseshoe Tavern
restaurants.description: A well-loved Marina dive bar known to regulars as 'The Shoe,' offering cold beers, a jukebox, pool tables, and multiple TVs for sports — a genuine no-frills SF institution.

restaurants.name: Bus Stop
restaurants.description: A low-key Cow Hollow bar with an old-school SF atmosphere, serving well-priced drinks and drawing a mixed crowd of long-time regulars and younger Union Street visitors.

restaurants.name: The Interval at Long Now
restaurants.type: Bar, café, and museum at Fort Mason
restaurants.description: A bar and café housed within the Long Now Foundation at Fort Mason, featuring an eclectic cocktail menu, natural wines, and rotating exhibits on long-term thinking in a stunning waterfront setting.
restaurants.address: 2 Marina Blvd, Bldg A, Fort Mason

restaurants.name: Radhaus
restaurants.description: A Fort Mason beerhall serving German-inspired food and a rotating selection of craft and imported beers in a spacious, communal setting with bay views on the Fort Mason campus.
restaurants.address: 2 Marina Blvd, Bldg A, Fort Mason

restaurants.name: Bar Darling
restaurants.description: A stylish cocktail bar on Chestnut Street known for its creative seasonal cocktail menu, intimate atmosphere, and quality spirits program drawing a discerning Marina crowd.

restaurants.name: Sully's Marina Lounge
restaurants.description: A popular Marina sports bar and lounge with a neighborhood-friendly vibe, multiple screens, and a full bar menu drawing locals for game days and weekend outings.

restaurants.name: The Black Horse London Pub
restaurants.description: One of San Francisco's smallest and most beloved bars, this cozy Union Street nook captures an authentic British pub atmosphere with a tight curated beer list and a famously intimate space for regulars.

restaurants.name: Peet's Coffee
restaurants.description: A popular local anchor on Chestnut Street's retail strip, Peet's serves the Bay Area coffee chain's signature dark-roast coffees and espresso drinks, a neighborhood morning staple.

restaurants.name: Roam Artisan Burgers
restaurants.description: A Marina outpost of the local burger mini-chain, serving grass-fed beef, bison, turkey, and veggie burgers with responsibly sourced ingredients and a focus on sustainability.

restaurants.name: Betelnut
restaurants.description: A longtime Union Street fixture, Betelnut serves Southeast and East Asian street-food-inspired dishes alongside an extensive cocktail and Asian beer menu in a bustling, vibrant dining room.

restaurants.name: Sweetgreen
restaurants.type: Health-focused salad and grain bowl chain
restaurants.description: A Chestnut Street location of the national salad-and-grain-bowl chain popular with the Marina's health-conscious crowd for customizable seasonal bowls and sourced-ingredient salads.

hotels.name: Hotel Drisco Pacific Heights
hotels.description: A 48-room 1903 Edwardian boutique hotel on a quiet Pacific Heights hilltop, celebrated for its complimentary gourmet breakfast, evening wine reception, private chauffeur service, and e-bike lending — a longtime local favorite for understated luxury.

hotels.name: Cow Hollow Inn & Suites
hotels.description: A well-situated motor inn on Lombard Street offering comfortable rooms and free self-parking — a practical choice for visitors who want walkable access to Union Street restaurants and Chestnut Street shops.

hotels.name: Infinity Hotel San Francisco, Tapestry Collection by Hilton
hotels.description: A Hilton Tapestry Collection property in the Marina District featuring rooftop fire pits, a zen garden, and spacious rooms within easy walking distance of Chestnut Street dining and the bay.

hotels.name: Hotel Del Sol
hotels.description: A colorful, family-friendly boutique motor inn with a heated outdoor pool and playful California-inspired décor set around a courtyard, a cheerful option near the Marina Green.

hotels.name: Seaside Inn
hotels.description: A no-frills, affordable inn in the Marina District within a 10-minute walk of Marina Green, Chestnut Street shops, and Union Street restaurants — a practical base for exploring the northern neighborhoods.

hotels.name: Marina Motel
hotels.description: One of the Marina's oldest motor courts, the Marina Motel features enclosed parking, a garden courtyard, and simple, well-maintained rooms a short walk from the waterfront.

hotels.name: Greenwich Inn San Francisco
hotels.description: A charming boutique inn on the edge of Pacific Heights and the Marina, offering comfortable rooms and a tour desk, a 9-minute walk from Fillmore Street's shops and restaurants.

hotels.name: Union Street Inn
hotels.description: An intimate bed and breakfast on Cow Hollow's Union Street, offering individually decorated rooms in a restored Edwardian building with a secluded garden and full breakfast each morning.

hotels.name: Pacific Heights Inn
hotels.description: A quiet, affordable motor inn in the residential edge of Pacific Heights and Cow Hollow, recommended for travelers wanting a peaceful alternative to the busier Lombard Street corridor.

hotels.name: Coventry Motor Inn
hotels.description: A well-located motor inn on Lombard Street offering straightforward, clean accommodations with free parking and easy access to the Marina, Cow Hollow, and Fisherman's Wharf.

shops.name: FLAX Art & Design
shops.description: A beloved San Francisco institution housed at Fort Mason Center, FLAX carries an extensive selection of fine art supplies, drafting materials, papers, and design goods for professionals and hobbyists alike.
shops.address: 2 Marina Blvd, Bldg D, Fort Mason

shops.name: Arion Press
shops.type: Fine press letterpress printer and bookshop
shops.description: A world-renowned fine-press letterpress printing studio and shop at Fort Mason Center, producing limited-edition artist books that are collected by libraries and private collectors internationally.
shops.address: 2 Marina Blvd, Bldg B, Fort Mason

shops.name: Taylor Stitch
shops.type: Men's sustainable clothing brand and flagship store
shops.description: San Francisco-founded Taylor Stitch sells durable, sustainability-focused men's clothing — shirts, denim, outerwear, and footwear — from its Chestnut Street flagship, emphasizing quality over fast fashion.

shops.name: Books Inc.
shops.description: A Marina outpost of San Francisco's beloved independent bookstore chain, Books Inc. carries a curated selection of fiction, nonfiction, children's books, and local authors with knowledgeable staff recommendations.

shops.name: Union Street Goldsmith
shops.description: A long-running Union Street jewelry studio where artisan goldsmiths design and fabricate custom fine jewelry on-site, with a gallery of ready-to-wear pieces in gold, platinum, and gemstones.

shops.name: Betsy Fisher
shops.description: A Union Street boutique curating contemporary women's clothing, accessories, and gifts from emerging and established designers, known for its personal styling approach and well-edited seasonal collections.

shops.name: Plumpjack Wine & Spirits
shops.description: The flagship retail shop of the Plumpjack Group, offering an expertly curated selection of California and international wines, craft spirits, and knowledgeable staff guidance in the heart of Cow Hollow.

shops.name: California Wine Merchant
shops.description: A neighborhood wine shop dedicated exclusively to California wines, with a broad selection spanning small-production Napa and Sonoma producers alongside coastal and Central Valley labels.

shops.name: Sanrio
shops.type: Japanese character goods and gifts store
shops.description: A well-stocked Chestnut Street Sanrio outpost carrying Hello Kitty and other Japanese character merchandise — stationery, accessories, plush toys, and gifts popular with shoppers of all ages.

shops.name: Zinc Details
shops.type: Modern home décor and design store
shops.description: A Cow Hollow design shop curating contemporary furniture, lighting, and home accessories from international designers, appreciated for its clean aesthetic and thoughtfully selected merchandise.

shops.name: Sur La Table
shops.description: A Chestnut Street outpost of the kitchen retail chain, stocking professional-grade cookware, bakeware, small appliances, and culinary tools, with regular cooking classes offered on-site.

shops.name: Ambiance
shops.description: A San Francisco–based women's clothing boutique with a Union Street location, known for its accessible mix of casual and dressy styles for everyday wear and special occasions.

artEntertainment.name: Palace of Fine Arts Theatre
artEntertainment.description: An intimate 1,000-seat theater housed within the iconic 1915 Palace of Fine Arts rotunda, hosting a diverse calendar of live music, comedy, dance, and theatrical performances throughout the year.

artEntertainment.name: Fort Mason Center for Arts & Culture
artEntertainment.description: A sprawling waterfront cultural campus at the edge of the Marina, hosting hundreds of events annually across theaters, galleries, and pavilions — from aerial arts festivals and craft fairs to exhibitions and improv comedy.

artEntertainment.name: BATS Improv
artEntertainment.description: The Bay Area's premier improvisational theater company, based at Fort Mason Center, offering weekly performances, jams, workshops, and special events in the intimate BATS Annex and main theater.

artEntertainment.name: Cowell Theater at Fort Mason
artEntertainment.description: A 440-seat performing arts theater at Fort Mason Center hosting dance, theater, film, and special events as part of the campus's vibrant year-round cultural programming.

artEntertainment.name: Gateway Pavilion at Fort Mason
artEntertainment.description: A large, flexible event and exhibition space at Fort Mason Center's Pier 2, used for major art installations, festivals, and public programs including the annual Aerial Arts Festival and West Coast Craft fairs.

artEntertainment.name: The Haas-Lilienthal House
artEntertainment.description: A beautifully preserved 1886 Queen Anne Victorian mansion in Pacific Heights operated by San Francisco Heritage, open for guided tours offering a vivid window into upper-class Gilded Age life in the city.

artEntertainment.name: Marina Green
artEntertainment.description: San Francisco's most iconic urban lawn, stretching along the bayfront with views of the Golden Gate Bridge, Alcatraz, and Marin — a gathering point for kite flying, outdoor movies, running, and community events.

artEntertainment.name: Alta Plaza Park
artEntertainment.description: A beautifully terraced Pacific Heights park atop a hill with sweeping views of the city and bay, popular for picnics, dog walking, tennis, and community gatherings.

artEntertainment.name: Lafayette Park
artEntertainment.description: A beloved Pacific Heights park offering tennis courts, off-leash dog runs, picnic lawns, and panoramic views of the bay and city skyline, a community anchor for the surrounding residential neighborhood.

artEntertainment.name: Wave Organ
artEntertainment.type: Sound sculpture and public art installation
artEntertainment.description: An acoustic sculpture at the tip of the Marina jetty consisting of 25 organ pipes that produce musical sounds as bay waves move through them — a free and unique sensory experience on the waterfront.

gymsRecreation.name: Yoga Flow SF — Union Street
gymsRecreation.description: A popular Cow Hollow yoga studio offering a wide range of yoga styles and workshops across multiple class times, set in an airy second-floor space with floor-to-ceiling windows on Union Street.

gymsRecreation.name: Karma Yoga
gymsRecreation.description: A neighborhood yoga studio at 2219 Filbert Street in Cow Hollow offering a consistent and community-focused yoga practice across a range of class levels and styles.

gymsRecreation.name: Hot 8 Yoga — Marina
gymsRecreation.description: A Marina location of the Hot 8 Yoga brand offering heated yoga classes in multiple styles — from Power and Vinyasa to Yin and Sculpt — known for its spa-clean facilities and community atmosphere.

gymsRecreation.name: CorePower Yoga — The Marina
gymsRecreation.type: Hot yoga and yoga sculpt studio
gymsRecreation.description: A Marina location of the national CorePower Yoga chain, offering heated power yoga, yoga sculpt, and restoration classes in a well-equipped studio near Chestnut Street.

gymsRecreation.name: Barre Union
gymsRecreation.description: A boutique Marina barre studio offering low-impact, high-intensity classes combining ballet barre technique with Pilates and strength training, popular with the neighborhood's fitness-focused community.

gymsRecreation.name: CORE40 Marina (Lagree Fitness)

gymsRecreation.name: Crunch Fitness — Marina
gymsRecreation.description: A Marina location of the national Crunch Fitness chain, offering a compact but well-equipped gym floor with cardio machines, free weights, and group fitness classes for members.

gymsRecreation.name: The Pad Studios
gymsRecreation.description: A boutique Marina movement studio offering yoga, stretching, and bodywork sessions designed to improve flexibility and mobility, with an approachable, personalized class environment.

gymsRecreation.name: Presidio YMCA

gymsRecreation.name: Marina Green Running Path & Bay Trail

gymsRecreation.name: Anchor Meditation
gymsRecreation.description: A Cow Hollow studio offering guided meditation classes, breathwork sessions, and mindfulness workshops in a calm, welcoming environment designed for both beginners and experienced practitioners.
